title: MM-MT102-SteerStatusTools

scope.summary:
GOAL: Give orchestrator-model sessions governed steering and observation tools over the workers they spawned: `steer_worker{child_session_id, message}`, `interrupt_worker{child_session_id}`, `worker_status{child_session_id}`, `list_children{}`. This is the async steering layer that the Anthropic multi-agent research system names as its own gap (their steering is synchronous-only); Handshake delivers steer messages through the MT-002 steer queue with per-transport capability awareness.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_tools/steer_tools.rs (+ types additions in model_tools/types.rs) registering the four tools on the same session tool channel as MT-101; delivery adapter that enqueues onto the MT-002 steer queue; a per-parent token-bucket rate limiter; ledger + FR-event stamping on every call. Tests. No frontend changes.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Scope of authority: a parent may only steer/interrupt/inspect its OWN children (lineage from the MT-103 registry once it lands; until then, from SpawnRequest.parent_session_id attribution in the coordinator/ledger). Any call naming a session that is not a live child of the caller returns typed `NotYourChild` — the tool must not even confirm whether the session exists (no session-id oracle).
2. steer_worker: validates message size (config cap, default 16 KiB), passes the message through the MT-104 injection-scan pipeline BEFORE enqueue (a quarantined message is not delivered; caller gets typed `MessageQuarantined` with the finding id), then enqueues onto the MT-002 steer queue addressed to the child session.
3. Capability-aware delivery (per-transport steer seams MT-023/043/062): app-server transport = mid-turn injection; claude transport = queued-turn (delivered at next turn boundary); acp transport = next-turn. worker_status exposes the delivery capability class so the orchestrator model knows WHEN its steer will land; the tool response includes `delivery_class: mid_turn | queued_turn | next_turn`.
4. interrupt_worker: requests cooperative cancellation of the child's current turn via the coordinator's CancellationToken plumbing — it NEVER kills the process directly and never bypasses SwarmCoordinator ownership of teardown; the child session survives (turn-level interrupt), and a policy flag (MT-106) controls whether a parent may interrupt at all.
5. worker_status: returns the child's session state (from the MT-001 session model / coordinator state), current turn state, last MT-121 signal if any, and queue depth of pending steers. list_children: returns live + recently-terminated children of the caller only, with role_id and lane.
6. Rate limits: per-parent token bucket (config: default 30 steer calls/min, 10 interrupts/min); exceeding returns typed `RateLimited` with retry_after_ms — the model gets a bounded, honest backoff signal instead of a silent drop (HBR-SWARM-002 no-silent-loss).
7. Ledger + events: every call (all four tools, allow and deny) writes a process_ledger row with parent attribution, tool name, target child, decision, and injection-scan verdict where applicable. Steer deliveries are recorded so a lost message is detectable (no-silent-loss).

SECURITY FRAME (binding): steering is inter-model content flow — a privilege-escalation and injection surface. All steer bodies are injection-scanned (MT-104); parent identity is server-side only (MT-101 rule); deny-by-default policy (MT-106) gates steer/interrupt capability per role pair; nothing here spawns sessions.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read MT-101 model_tools module, MT-002 steer-queue contract, per-transport steer seams (MT-023/043/062 contracts), coordinator CancellationToken usage.
2. Add SteerWorkerInput/Output, InterruptWorkerInput/Output, WorkerStatusOutput, ListChildrenOutput, and typed errors NotYourChild, MessageQuarantined, RateLimited, PolicyDenied to model_tools/types.rs.
3. Implement steer_tools.rs handlers with lineage check, policy check, injection scan, queue enqueue, capability-class resolution.
4. Implement the per-parent token-bucket limiter (in-memory keyed by parent_session_id, config-driven caps).
5. Ledger + FR stamping with parent attribution on every path.
6. Tests per expected_tests.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except named IPC/GUI surfaces for the GUI MT; this MT names none)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/coordinator.rs (read-only; interrupt goes through existing cancellation plumbing, no new teardown path)
acceptance_criteria: All four tools (steer_worker, interrupt_worker, worker_status, list_children) exist on the session tool channel, gated behind the same model_to_model feature flag family as MT-101.
A parent can only address its own children: cross-lineage calls return typed NotYourChild without confirming target existence (anti-oracle), with a dedicated test.
Every steer message passes the MT-104 injection scan before enqueue; a crafted instruction-shaped message is quarantined, not delivered, and the caller receives MessageQuarantined.

Delivery is via the MT-002 steer queue only — no direct writes into a child's transport; worker_status reports the correct delivery_class per transport (mid_turn for app-server, queued_turn for claude, next_turn for acp).
interrupt_worker cancels the child's current turn via coordinator cancellation plumbing; the child process/session is not killed and coordinator teardown ownership is untouched.
Per-parent rate limits enforce configured caps and return typed RateLimited with retry_after_ms; no call is silently dropped.
Every call on every path (success, NotYourChild, PolicyDenied, MessageQuarantined, RateLimited) produces a process_ledger row with parent attribution.
expected_tests: unit: message size cap enforcement; unknown child id => NotYourChild
unit: token bucket refill math and per-parent isolation
integration: steer enqueued onto MT-002 queue with correct delivery_class per transport
integration: quarantined message never reaches the queue; finding recorded
integration: interrupt cancels current turn, session stays alive, ledger row written
negative: policy denies interrupt for a role pair configured no-interrupt (MT-106)
implementation_notes: Lineage source order: MT-103 registry when present; fallback to coordinator/ledger parent_session_id attribution so this MT is testable before MT-103 merges (document the fallback in code).

delivery_class mapping is a capability lookup, not a behavior reimplementation: the actual mid-turn/queued-turn/next-turn mechanics live in the per-transport steer MTs (MT-023 app-server, MT-043 claude, MT-062 acp); this MT only routes and reports.
Rate limiter is in-memory and per-process by design (steering is coordinator-local); note this limitation for any future multi-process coordinator work.
Operator precedence: the operator's own steering surfaces (operator_chat) are NOT rate-limited or policy-gated by this MT; only model-initiated calls flow through these tools.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-001 session model, MT-002 steer queue, MT-023/043/062 per-transport steer, MT-104 injection scan, MT-106 policy, MT-121 signals.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend tools; the live steering feed and operator entry points ship in MT-107.

target_entries: Model-to-model orchestration: steer/interrupt/status/list_children tools — lineage scope, delivery classes per transport, rate limits, quarantine behavior

risk_if_missed: Spawned workers are fire-and-forget: no mid-run correction, no bounded interrupt, no status introspection — the orchestrator either polls (operator-declared defect) or loses control of children, and steering content flows unscanned if improvised later.

risks: RISK-1: Cross-lineage steering — a parent steers or interrupts another parent's child (or an operator session) by guessing session ids, escalating one compromised orchestrator into swarm-wide control.
RISK-2: Injection relay — a compromised or manipulated orchestrator embeds instruction-shaped content in steer messages, turning steering into a prompt-injection channel into workers.
RISK-3: Steer flooding — an orchestrator in a defective loop floods a child with steers, burning tokens and starving the queue (unbounded loop).
RISK-4: Interrupt as kill — interrupt_worker implemented as process termination bypasses coordinator teardown, leaking leases/worktrees and violating STOP semantics.
RISK-5: Session-id oracle — differing errors for 'not found' vs 'not yours' let a model enumerate live session ids.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Server-side lineage check on every call; NotYourChild typed error; dedicated cross-lineage test.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Mandatory MT-104 injection scan before enqueue; quarantine blocks delivery; test with a crafted instruction-shaped message.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Per-parent token-bucket rate limits with typed RateLimited + retry_after_ms; caps operator-configurable; test proves enforcement.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Interrupt routes through coordinator CancellationToken turn-cancel only; coordinator.rs is read-only for this MT; test asserts session alive after interrupt.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Identical NotYourChild response for nonexistent and non-owned targets, asserted by test.

research_provenance.source: Direct source inspection 2026-07-21 of wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1: coordinator.rs (CancellationToken per-session cancel), model_lane.rs (ModelLaneStore transport/lane metadata), events.rs (FR-EVT-SWARM catalogue), process_ledger/ (attribution rows). Cross-family seams from WP-017 stub: MT-002 steer queue, MT-023/043/062 per-transport steer capability classes. External precedent: Anthropic multi-agent research system names synchronous-only steering as their gap — this MT is the async steering they lack; Claude Code marker-line injection defense copied via MT-104.
